SUSTAINABLE WATER
MASTER PLAN  Recommended Action
  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Adopt a finding of no possibility of significant effect pursuant to
  Section 15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption) of the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines and a finding of
  categorical exemption pursuant to Section 15307 of the CEQA
  Guidelines; and
  2. Receive and provide direction on the 2026 Sustainable Water Master
  Plan Update.

  Dr. Mark Gold and Sunny Wang, Water Utilities Manager, made a
  presentation and responded to questions posed by the City Council regarding
  the City’s progress toward local water self-sufficiency, noting that Santa
  Monica is currently at approximately 80–85% local supply due to projects
  such as SWIP, Arcadia Plant efficiency upgrades, Olympic Well Field
  restoration, and citywide AMI deployment. They highlighted updated
  groundwater sustainability limits (roughly 9,000–10,000 AFY instead of the
  previously assumed 15,000 AFY), the projected future supply-demand gap
  driven by growth and climate impacts, and evaluated five alternatives:
  enhanced conservation, maximizing local reuse via direct potable reuse
  (DPR), airport groundwater remediation, regional potable-reuse/exchange
  partnerships, and potential future seawater desalination. Staff recommended
  a “portfolio” approach with near-term focus on conservation and DPR, and
  long-term exploration of regional partnerships and any future, technically
  and financially viable desalination.

  Motion by Mayor Torosis, seconded by Councilmember Raskin, to: (1) adopt
  a finding of no possibility of significant effect pursuant to CEQA’s
  common-sense exception; (2) receive and file the Sustainable Water Master
  Plan Update; and (3) direct staff to implement the near-term portfolio by fully
  advancing the 2024 Water Conservation Master Plan and proceeding with
  planning and design for a DPR connection from SWIP through the Olympic
  Advanced Water Treatment Plant to the Arcadia Water Treatment Plant (up
  to a 10% contribution, consistent with 2023 DPR regulations), and to pursue
  the long-term portfolio by initiating formal discussions with the Metropolitan
  Water District (regarding Pure Water SoCal and potential exchanges) and the
  City of Los Angeles (regarding Pure Water LA/Hyperion, possible recharge
  of the Charnock well field, and potential shared underground treatment
  facilities at or near the airport), while continuing to monitor (a) remediation
  progress and future production potential in the Santa Monica Airport

AFTER-ACTION  Staff recommends that the City Council review and comment on the

  2025 Palisades Fire and windstorm and answered Council questions. Staff
  reported key strengths, including early EOC activation, proactive Fire
  up-staffing and monitoring, effective Police curfew and evacuation support,
  strong public communications, and rapid debris removal by Public Works,
  and key challenges, including leadership absences, limited Council
  familiarity with disaster roles, some interagency communication issues, and

  planning group, an SMFD up-staffing and recall policy, enhanced web
  resources, the Community Connect platform, and additional leadership
  training.
